html:
The Warao are a people of the Orinoco delta in eastern Venezuela, with smaller groups in Guyana and Suriname. Their name is often translated as boat people. Their language is an isolate, related to no other known language.

They live in houses on stilts over the delta's channels and travel by dugout canoe. For many groups the moriche palm was the staff of life: its starch was food, and its fibres gave hammocks and rope. Other groups grew taro and, later, worked for missions and sawmills.

The Warao had early contact with Europeans at the mouth of the Orinoco, and with their neighbours the Lokono and Kalina. With some tens of thousands of people they are one of Venezuela's largest Indigenous peoples. In the 2010s, during the Venezuelan crisis, many Warao families fled to Brazil.
